title: Longitudinal tracking of T cell lymphomas in mice using flow cytometry
protocol: Dissect spleens into dissection medium kept on ice or at 18°C–23°C.
Transfer individual spleens into a well of a 6-well plate.
Add 4 mL of 18°C–23°C dissection medium to each spleen.
Finely chop spleens into 15 or more pieces using a scalpel with a fresh blade.
Add 1 mL of 5–10 mg/mL Collagenase type IV, resulting in a final concentration of 1–2 mg/mL.
Incubate the mixture in a 37°C incubator (5% CO2) for 25–30 min.
Stop the reaction by adding 2 mM EDTA.
Pass spleens through a 40 μm cell strainer, placed on top of a 50 mL conical tube.
Facilitate this process using the plunger of a 20 mL syringe to mash tissue through the mesh.
Rinse through with 2 mL ice cold flow cytometry buffer.
Allow the cell strainer to drain and repeat 1–2 more times.
Pellet immune cells by centrifuging at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend cell pellets in 2 mL chilled (4°C) flow cytometry buffer by gently vortexing.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Aliquot ∼2–5 × 10^5 cells from each single cell suspension into a well of a 96-well v-bottom tissue culture plate (plate A).
Keep the plate on ice or at 4°C for further protocol steps.
Centrifuge plate A and plate B at 500 × g for 4 min in a 4°C benchtop centrifuge equipped with a microplate holder to pellet the cells.
Remove the supernatant by flicking the plate into a sink following a single continuous motion.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL live/dead blue stain through gentle repetitive pipetting.
Incubate at 4°C for 10–15 min.
Top up wells with 100 μL 4°C flow cytometry buffer and centrifuge (500 × g at 4°C) for 4 min.
Remove the supernatant through aspiration or by flicking the plate into a sink following a single continuous motion.
Add 100 μL/well flow cytometry buffer and centrifuge (500 × g at 4°C) to pellet cells.
Remove the supernatant through aspiration or by flicking the plate into a sink following a single continuous motion.
Resuspend cells from plate A in 75 μL/well staining panel A – extracellular antibody panel.
Resuspend cells from plate B in 75 μL/well staining panel B – extracellular antibody panel.
Perform surface staining for 30–60 min at 4°C in the dark.
Top up wells in plate A with 125 μL 4°C PBS and centrifuge (500 × g at 4°C) for 4 min.
Remove the supernatant through aspiration or by flicking the plate into a sink following a single continuous motion.
Resuspend plate A in 75 μL BD Cytofix Fixation buffer and incubate for 10–15 min at 4°C.
Top up wells in plate A with 125 μL ice cold PBS and centrifuge (500 × g at 4°C) for 4 min.
Remove the supernatant through aspiration or by flicking the plate into a sink following a single continuous motion.
Resuspend samples in plate A with 150 μL PBS.
Top up wells in plate B with 125 μL of 4°C PBS.
Centrifuge plate B at 500 × g and 4°C for 4 minutes.
Remove the supernatant through aspiration or flicking the plate into a sink following a single continuous motion.
Resuspend plate B in 75 μL/well fix/perm solution and incubate at 4°C in the dark for 20–30 minutes.
Centrifuge plate B at 500 × g and 4°C for 4 minutes.
Remove the supernatant through aspiration or flicking the plate into a sink following a single continuous motion.
Top up wells in plate B with 125 μL ice cold Perm/wash buffer.
Centrifuge plate B at 500 × g and 4°C for 4 minutes.
Remove the supernatant through aspiration or flicking the plate into a sink following a single continuous motion.
Resuspend samples in plate B with 75 μL perm/wash buffer.
Top up wells in plate B with 75 μL PBS.
Acquire flow cytometry data on a 4 laser BD Fortessa flow cytometer with high throughput sample loader.
Keep fixed samples at 18°C–23°C during the protocol.
Store fixed samples in the dark to prevent degradation.
Optional: Pass samples through a 40 μm cell strainer prior to acquisition.
Use Pall AcroPrep 96-well 40 μm Filter plates for high-throughput sample straining.
Prepare flow cytometry compensation controls using UltraComp eBeads™ Plus Compensation Beads according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Calibrate the BD Fortessa and optimize voltages.
Set up acquisition parameters and plate labels in BD FACSDiva software.
Create an acquisition worksheet in FACSDiva for visualizing sample acquisition.
Visualize dot plots showing a basic gating structure with total lymphocytes (FSC vs. SSC).
Live cells (viability dye-negative in FSC vs. viability dye).
Singlet cells (FSC-A vs. FSC-H).
Congenic markers CD45.1 vs. CD45.2.
Set up plate on high-throughput screen (HTS) mode on the BD Fortessa.
Test sample flow rate using <5 μL spare sample and adjust if necessary to achieve a flow rate of 1,000–5,000 events/second.
Acquire and record data from all samples.
Export data as an .FCS file following acquisition of samples.
Import files into FlowJo.
Create and apply a compensation matrix using single color compensation controls.
Apply the compensation matrix to experimental samples.
Analyze data in FlowJo software.
